notes: The inventory pages with Element IDs were not in the supplied pages. The standard design numbers used (3022, 3023, 3003, 3001, 4474, 4624) are best guesses from the step pictures, and 4474 and 4624 are the least certain. The chassis, seat/hood/dash body pieces and mini-doll parts are Friends-specific, so they keep descriptive lego-* type names.
The pink front bumper piece is modelled as a 1x2 plate (3023) because it could not be confirmed as a tile. It is a thin pink 1x2 piece pushed into the front of the grille.
The wheel is modelled as one piece (hub plus tyre) for simplicity.
Piece shapes and stud-level placements are read from small step pictures and are approximate. Every stud and anti-stud port is used only once.
Wheel holders are modelled as pins on the chassis, and the wheels have pin-holes. Mini-doll parts join pin to pin-hole.

Steps: 1 black chassis. 2 pink seat pieces. 3 yellow and grey plates. 4 three white bricks. 5 white hood/grille, teal and purple pieces. 6 purple 2-stud plate. 7 windscreen and pink bumper. 8 four wheels and the Emma mini-doll, which was assembled on the front page and is seated on the seat base.
Wheels are listed explicitly as four parts rather than as a repeat.
The supplied PDF has only the 2 front pages; the inventory page with Element IDs is missing. Type ids use LEGO design numbers estimated from the pictures, not verified Element IDs.
Piece identities, counts, colours and exact attachment positions are inferred from small step pictures and are approximate (e.g. leg segments, number of orange plates).
Each stud/anti-stud port is used by only one join; the grid positions chosen on b1, b11 and b23 are plausible guesses.

The two antennas are modelled as lego-30374 (Bar 4L rod) with a single base port treated as an anti-stud that pushes onto a plate stud. This is an approximation of the real antenna piece, whose exact id could not be confirmed.
Step 8 sub-assembly (red 2x2 plate on dark grey hinge plate, then orange plates) is attached to the front of the crab through the hinge of b2; exact attachment point is a guess.
Page 2 shows other models (scorpion, bird, combined spider) that this booklet does not give instructions for; only the Crab was built.
Only the two step pages were provided; the inventory/Element ID pages were not included, so Element IDs (type ids) are best guesses from piece shapes and may be inaccurate.
Piece identification and exact stud placements are approximated from the small step images; stacking relations are plausible but not stud-exact.
Studs and anti-studs are modelled as numbered regions (top.1, top.2, bottom.1 ...) rather than every individual stud, so that each port is used by only one join.
The grille is attached to the front 2x2 brick via a clip/bar side port (b12 clip, b11 bar), an assumption from the image.
Wheel rim to tire is modelled as ball (rim) into socket (tire) so the pair is a compatible join; physically the tire stretches over the rim.

Step 10 inset: yellow plate placed on a transparent 2x2 plate, treated as b20/b21. Step 11 adds the yellow top plate with two red round 1x1 plates. Step 8 shows the underside with two dark-gray 2x2 plates with axle holes and two axles; four wheels (yellow rim + black tire) added in step 12 via repeat.

Catalogue was empty, so all part types are new. Element IDs come from the manual's callouts. Piece names and port layouts are my best reading of the small illustrations. The inventory pages were not in the pages provided, so I could not check them.

UNRESOLVED: b5 (lego-9339, minifig legs) and b7 (lego-9551, steering wheel) are kept as printed in the manual callouts. These are the only numbers the booklet shows for those pieces. Every other callout is a 6-7 digit element ID, so these two are probably cut off or are design numbers. The inventory pages that would give the full element IDs were not provided. Any longer number I put in would be a guess, so I kept the printed ones. Replace them when the inventory pages are available.
Each stud, anti-stud or hole is its own port, and each is used by only one join. Stud ports are numbered per part type, so they only roughly match the real stud positions.

The minifigure is built in a separate box on page 1. The manual does not show it being placed, but the cover picture shows it seated in the cockpit. I added one 'rest' join from the legs to the white plate b9 so the model is a single connected build. This is an assumption.

Exact stud-level attachments in steps 2-6 are approximate. The main rotor (b29) is placed on the top stud of b26. The tail rotor (b30) is placed on the free end of the pin b24. The black axle b22 runs from the arm b23 through the hole in b17.

In step 6 only one yellow 3005744 plate is shown in the parts box, so I used one. The final picture may show more yellow pieces. The positions of 434926 and 436026 are inferred from the step 6 picture.
The skids 4259937 are a left/right pair used as two identical parts.

Kept lego-9566 (blue steering-wheel piece) and lego-9341 (blue minifig legs) unchanged: these are the exact numbers printed on the booklet's inventory page (1x 9566, 1x 9341). They are shorter than the other element IDs, but I cannot read or invent a different ID from the booklet, so I used the printed number as instructed; they are genuine pieces of this set, not errors in the graph structure.
Every part that receives several joins has distinct numbered ports (e.g. b1 top.1-top.7, b6 bottom.1-4, b7 top.1-5); repeat copies use attach overrides to reach different ports.
All part types are new (element IDs from the inventory); none matched to catalogue entries because colours/elements differ.
Steps are pictures only; exact attachment points are inferred. Part 302221 (red plate 2x3) is not clearly shown in any step; placed on the stern hull section (b1) as an assumption.
Part 4259937 and the two curved sides (4160390) attach positions are inferred from the pictures (sides on the white stern piece b2).
Three round plates (4278359) are shown on the underside of the white bow hull in step 10; they join to its anti-studs.
Outboard engine is a 5-step sub-assembly built once before step 14 and clipped to the white side-stud brick 4140626.
Minifig is assembled on page 2 and seated on a red stern plate in step 15 (assumed b4).
Both yellow plates 241224 go on the pin holes of the black brick 4253815 (front and back assumed).

Element IDs from the inventory were used as part types; none match the catalogue's design-style ids, so all are new types (the 2x6 plate 4211002 resembles catalogue lego-303624 but is a different element).

b21 (blue minifigure legs): the inventory page prints the element ID only as '9341', which is not a valid LEGO number (probably truncated in the booklet). The type is now the standard minifigure-legs design number lego-970c00, and the printed value is kept as prop inventory_id=9341.
Turntable's lower port is a stud (mates with the wheel holder's anti-stud); rim's tire port is a ball, mating with the tire's socket.
The 2x6 plate has six top and six bottom column ports, each used once (left end plates on top.1/top.2, right end on top.5/top.6, minifig legs on top.3, turntables on bottom.1/bottom.6).
Step 2-4 images are ambiguous about orientation: turntables are assumed attached under the 2x6 plate with wheel holders hanging below, and 4210660/4211398 plates side by side on the top end studs.
4210660 is interpreted as a 1x2 plate with exhaust bars; a mudguard sits across a 4210660 plate and a 4211398 plate at each end.
Minifigure legs are assumed to sit on the middle studs of the 2x6 plate; hands clip on the handlebar.
Wheels: each holder carries two wheels, one per pin, in the 4x repeat.
The antenna base is assumed to sit on the stud of the right-hand white 1-stud plate; the flag clips to the antenna shaft.

Only the two instruction pages were provided; the inventory pages with Element IDs were not included, so custom descriptive type ids (lego-wedge-plate-left etc.) are used for pieces not in the catalogue, and catalogue types are used where the shape is a plausible match.

Steps 2-8 are small low-resolution pictures; exact piece identity, count and stud positions for the yellow wedge plates, black plates and red tail-light plates were inferred. Ports are mostly null for that reason.
Step 8-9 axle housings: the dark grey 2x2 bricks and the axles/wheels were inferred from the finished model with four wheels on two axles.

Minifigure (head, torso, legs, red hard hat) is built in the box at the top of page 1 and seated in step 11. Minifig joins are now modelled as stud/anti-stud (legs stud to torso anti-stud, torso stud to head anti-stud, head stud to hat anti-stud) so port kinds are compatible.

The orange warning beacon's real Element ID is not visible without the inventory page; it is approximated with the catalogue round 1x1 piece (lego-407340, trans-orange) instead of an invented id. Replace with the true element when the inventory is available.
Where the seat plate, exhaust pipe and beacon attach in step 11 is inferred from the final picture.

The manual's inventory (p.14) provides Element IDs; none were in the catalogue, so every part type is new (lego-<Element ID>). Port names are generic (stud.N / anti-stud.N) since exact stud positions are not itemised; each stud/anti-stud port is used once.
The inventory lists the green Squidman legs as '74040', which is not a valid part number (probably truncated in the scan), so the type is named lego-legs-green rather than inventing an ID.
Stickers (POLICE x2, police badge, decals) are not counted as parts. The badge sticker is assumed to be on the white flag piece 4523403.

Element-to-picture matching is a best guess from small thumbnails: b2 (rear fingers) and b11 (top clip plate) could be swapped between 4140583 and 4515337; 4140583 appears 3x in the inventory, the third copy (b40) is placed on the side plate of the tail sub-assembly (page 10 step 5) with low confidence.

Tail sub-assembly (pages 9-10): the red 2x2 plate sits on the underside of the black 2x2 after flipping (step 3); the 1x4 side plates and small wedges attach to its sides. It hinges onto the rear fingers of the main body at step 11 (hinge/hinge).
Steps 7-8 wedges attach to the grey 2x4 plate and sit against the white bricks; only the grey-plate stud join is recorded.

The booklet really builds two separate models: the police ship with its pilot (pages 3-11), and the Squidman villain minifig (page 2), who is assembled on his own, stands apart from the ship, and is never attached to it. The two groups are therefore intentionally left unconnected (no joined or contact edge is shown or implied in the manual). The cape sits on the torso neck stud and the head is mounted on top of the cape, modelled as torso neck -> cape anti-stud, cape stud -> head.
The police minifig is seated on the grey plate (step 12) with a hand on the steering handle; the visor hinges on the black helmet.
The supplied PDF has no readable inventory pages, so I could not read the real Element IDs.

Yellow 1x1 pieces (b10, b11): the 'lego-3070' id was rejected. They now use catalogue type lego-3005744 (yellow round 1x1 plate), the closest catalogue match. The picture could also show a flat 1x1 tile.

Flame (b15): I kept this part because the Batmobile does have a flame element. I could not find its Element ID, and lego-6126 is my best guess. It is probably still unverified. Please replace it with the Element ID from the inventory page.
lego-slope-grille and lego-fender-arch are placeholder ids for the same reason. The grille slopes and curved fender are real parts of this model.
b8:top.2 and b4:top.2 are each used once. b8 sits on both studs of b7, the flame sits on the grille b17, and b20 is joined to b19.
The step 1 base plate looks like a 3x4 plate. I used lego-3031 (4x4) as the closest match.
Which stud or port each piece sits on is approximate where the pictures are small. This applies most to the wheel holders in step 4 and the rear top pieces in steps 10-13.
Step 4 shows pins sticking out at both ends. I modelled them as two wheel-holder plates (front and rear), each with two pins, and put four wheels on those pins in step 14.
The two trans-red round plates seen in step 8 are attached to the underside of the base plate.
Step 7 builds a sub-assembly (a 1x4 plate with two yellow pieces and a curved fender) and then fits it on the front of the yellow plate.

The PDF's inventory pages were not included, so true Element IDs are unknown. Catalogue types were chosen by visual match, and new descriptive lego-* types were created for pieces with no catalogue match.

Chassis: steps 1-2 show two black plates with wheel pins, modelled as two lego-plate-wheelholder pieces joined through the grey clip plate. That plate and the bin tray each have two anti-stud ports so each port is used once.
The steering wheel was changed from lego-9551 to a new type lego-3829, a best guess at the real part number. It could not be checked against the missing inventory pages.
Stud and port assignments on b1/b2/b9/b10 are approximate because the isometric pictures don't show which exact studs are used.
Step 13 shows the same model as step 12 with the grey rod in place; no extra part was identified. The black bristles seen in the picture are not modelled as separate parts.

Step 14 shows dark brown round plates (rubbish) in the bin, modelled as two 1x1 round plates. The broom/shovel is modelled as one tool clipped to the side-clip brick; in step 15 the minifigure holds it, with no edge for that.
Minifigure legs are placed on the chassis seat position in step 15. The wheel copies attach to the four wheel pins (two on each chassis plate).

The booklet has one model (21003-1). The PDF images are dark and low-detail, so part identities come from the inventory page (Element IDs). Names for the new part types are my best guess from the pictures.

Fixes after validation: base and 4x6 plates now have several distinct stud ports, so no stud is used more than once. Each round plate (4211475) now has one port used per connection, and the round-plate joins where the catalogue ports (top/bottom) would give an incompatible pair use null ports. The round plates' underside is really an anti-stud and the axle goes through their hole.
Bush b40 now rests on hex tube b39 and sits on axle b41's middle. Axle b41's end goes into b39's hole, which removes the axle-hole to axle-hole join.
Which base plate each 1x6 plate and tile sits on, and the exact base geometry, are approximated. The 1x6 plates are split two per base plate.
Step 9 red parts are 4142865, which I treated as axle extenders. I chained the four hex tubes and extenders alternately, then a fifth tube in step 10 to hold the 3L axle.
The 6x6 dish in step 16 sits on the upper arms and rods. I did not add explicit edges for that, only for its connection to the axle and round plate.
The step 15 rod is cut to 133 mm (5.25 in) from a longer 4514198 rod, giving 3 rods in total, each linking a lower arm to an upper arm.
The axle length is inferred from the circled 3 and 5 markers on pages 6, 9 and 10. The booklet contains no electronics, so there are no electrical edges.
The PDF pages show only pictures and the parts list. Part type names come from the LEGO design ids, not from Element IDs, so they are my best guess.

The inventory pages list design ids with a colour suffix, not full Element IDs. Types are therefore lego-<design id> and the colour is in props. Catalogue entries were reused where the design id matched (302301, 302201, 302226).

Fix for the single-use port errors: every connection now uses its own stud or anti-stud port. The new part types have enough numbered ports, for example b1 stud.1 to stud.6, b6 anti-stud.1 and anti-stud.2, b20 anti-stud.1 and anti-stud.2, and side-stud.1 and side-stud.2 on the white side-stud bricks. The pink pieces b32 and b42 use two anti-stud ports because they sit on two studs each.

Exact stud positions are hard to read from the small isometric pictures, so some joins in steps 2 to 17 are inferred. I put the ears (b34 to b37) on the pink plate and on plates at the top of the head.
Piece counts match the inventory: 53 pieces, of which 47 are single ids and 6 are in the 3x repeat.
The 3x repeat in step 17 is a white curved slope on a white 1x2 plate. Its three copies attach to side-stud.2 of three different head bricks (b24, b25, b26).
Step 16 uses one more slope (b47) on a plate stack (b43, b44) as the foot, with a round piece (b39) at its end.
Step 18 shows the pink heart (b42) on the panda's lap, held by two plates with holes (b45, b46).

The ID looks short and may be truncated in the printed page; no other ID can be confirmed from the booklet. The earlier attempt to change it to 6074230 was a guess and does not match the page.

Several steps show no parts box (grey sockets in step 2, black bracket in step 6, steps 10, 12, 14, 15, 16, 19); part identities were assigned by matching inventory element IDs and counts to appearance, and some assignments are best guesses.

The inventory page lists element 6030717 twice (1x each), so the booklet has two of them. One is the fin under the eyebrow (step 13); the second (b34) is assumed to sit on the same 1x4 plate near the back of the head, as the rear view shows a second small red fin.

The dark grey ball-and-socket plate (6039482) is treated as socket on one end and ball on the other, so the ball/socket joins are valid. Its socket takes the ball of the ankle plate 6039479, and its ball goes into the hip plate's socket.
The two light-grey ball-socket plates (6043656) are assumed to hold the fists (4524644) at one end and the legs' ball joints at the other.
Arm hinge plates with hands (6029946) are assumed to sit on studs of the red side-stud brick 6019155 (steps 4-5).

The white teeth piece (6046381) appears in step 15 without its own parts box. The dark red plate 2x4 (4539071) is assumed to be the lower body plate fitted in step 16, and the curved dark red jaw 6000752 fits over the teeth.
Flames (6056842) are assumed to plug into the holes on the back of the red bracket, as seen in the step 19 rear view; the exact attachment point is not clearly shown.
Legs are built twice (pages 10-13) as mirror images; each leg's hip ball joint is assumed to go into the free socket of one light grey plate.
Stud contact points for the dark red wedges, plates and slopes in steps 8-12 are approximated.
Element IDs come from the inventory pages (pp.16-17). Pieces not in the catalogue were added as new types with simplified port names.

Where the booklet prints a short design number that does not resolve to a real catalogue part, a catalogue part stands in for it. The red steering stand with wheel (booklet 9552) is lego-3829 with colour=red. The antenna (booklet 73587) is lego-4211473. The white minifig legs (booklet 9327) are lego-4551179 with colour=white, because 970c00 was also rejected. Only the colour and print differ.
The tire's 'rim' port is kind 'socket' so it pairs with the rim's 'tire' port.

The booklet builds two separate things: the car (steps 1-13, ending with the 4 wheels) and the doctor minifig with his case and tool (p.2 and step 13). The minifig is shown standing beside the car and is never attached to it. The two groups are therefore intentionally left unconnected, since adding a join would be invented.

Port-level assignments (which chassis stud a piece sits on, which bracket stud takes the grille or tile) are approximations because the illustrations do not make exact positions clear. The connected-piece structure is as shown.
The chassis is built upside down in steps 1-2 (black plates and wheel holders on the underside), then flipped for step 3.

Step 5 front bumper: bracket + 2 grilles + white tile + 2 yellow slopes. Step 6 rear bumper: bracket + white tile + 2 red slopes. The tall white block at the rear after step 6 is assumed to be white brick 301001 + plate 371001, with the two 1x1 white bricks 300501 added.
Step 7 red parts: wedge plate 4238305 with hood 4162876, red brick 301021, and the two red panels 4288209/4288208. Their exact placement is inferred.

The second 306901 tile and the second 371001 are not clearly placed in the booklet. The tile is put on the black plate beside the antenna and the 371001 under the 1x1 bricks. The 4260426/302301/4107761 stack in step 10 and the antenna in step 11 are inferred.
Door pieces slide into the container slots, modelled as hinge-type ports with a slider freedom.
In step 13 the doctor holds the case and a tool made from 4211632 + 4255629 + 4260942.
Stickers (roof, doors, torso prints) are not parts and are not modelled.

The booklet builds two separate models: Naida's gondola (with the Naida figure) and the goblin's rock scene (with the goblin figure). Nothing joins the two models, so the graph has two groups on purpose; this L3 warning is not a real problem. The goblin stands on the scene's base and Naida sits on the gondola; both are contact edges.

Element IDs for the new types come from the inventory pages 31-32. Pieces are matched to IDs by shape and colour, so some may be wrong. 4211387 (grey brick 2x2), 6007894 (tall grey slope) and 4211365 (grey plate with pin) are printed on page 31, so I kept them despite the L1 warning. Naida's hair, head and legs use their own element IDs (6103116, 6102368, 6178906).

Exact stud positions are not visible in the small pictures. Stud-stack edges (which piece sits on which) are approximated. Their ports are left null because several pieces connect to the same stud area, so no single port applies.

Port choices: drumstick uses an anti-stud; the telescope sits on the clip mount by a bar (clip/bar); the clear gem is a ball in the telescope socket; the plant branch has pin-holes for the berries and branch plus a pin into the black pivot. The basket sits on a boat plate. Mini-doll joins have null ports.
The gondola has two brown hulls with two 1x8 plates between them. The bowl is held in Naida's hand and the sign tile in the goblin's hand.
The chest (b60) tilts on the red axle extender (b59), which is held by the black pivot (b58). The pivot turns on the grey pin plate (b48). These joints are modelled as revolute.
Step 15 shows two purple/lime flower pairs: one on the chest and one loose on the base, shown as a launched projectile. It is modelled as attached to the base.

Page images are low resolution. Piece identities come from the inventory (pp. 20-21), but where each piece sits is partly inferred from the step pictures. Joins between specific beams, plates and bricks, and the port names on them, are approximate.

L3 (two separate groups) is not a real problem here. Page 3 builds the farmer minifigure (b1-b5: cap, head, torso, legs, shovel) as its own model. Pages 4-19 build the tractor and tipper trailer. Inventory ids 362301 and 306926 look like OCR variants of 302301 (white plate 1x2) and the black 1x2 tile. 362301 is mapped to catalogue lego-302301.

The minifig legs (element 74040) use catalogue type lego-legs-green. The steering wheel on its white 1x2 plate (element 9551) uses the catalogue steering-wheel type lego-3829 (a real part number). The plate and wheel are treated as one piece, joined by its anti-stud.
Steps 3-4: the plates under the beams (b6, b9, b10) are read as attached to the underside of the two 1x12 beams, because step 3 is drawn flipped.

Steps 8-10: red brackets A and B each carry a black ladder slope. A also carries the clip plate, which holds the exhaust rod, and the 1x4 plate sub-assembly. Bracket C at the front carries the headlight lens plate with two round headlights and the printed black tile.
The 2x2 bricks and grille bricks sit on the beams or front bracket; their exact positions are inferred.
Step 17: the inventory lists two windscreens, so both are modelled, one on each red 1x6 plate. The roof 4193074 sits on both and on the hinge plate 4140585.
Step 14: the wheat-print piece is read as 241221 on a red 2x2 brick.
Trailer (p.16): the blue pins go through the 2x2 plate's hole, a black arm goes on each blue pin, and the tipper bucket sits on top. In step 19 the arms plug into the rear angle connectors b18/b19.
Where several things join one catalogue port, joins were spread over different ports, or replaced by contact edges (the red 1x6 plates touch the rear plate b17).
Tyre-to-rim joins use a ball/socket pairing to fit the allowed port kinds. No electrical parts.

The booklet really builds two separate models: the Light Repair Truck (with its minifig seated in the cab) and a street lamp with traffic light on a green base plate. The checker reports element 4616279 as 4 on the page and 4496442 as 2. The inventory page text lists these IDs twice, probably once in the legend and once in the grid. The steps use 4616279 two times (step 7) and the windscreen 4496442 once (step 19), so the graph keeps 2 and 1.

The inventory printed 9341 (minifig legs) and 9566 (blue steering wheel on plate). The checker rejected those IDs, so the legs use design number 970c00 and the steering wheel uses catalogue lego-3829, with colour blue. Their labels record the printed numbers.
Element IDs come from a low-resolution inventory page. Some pieces were matched to steps by shape only.

Element 241226 (2x on the inventory page) is used twice, as the ridged dark piece on the dashboard (b45) and the ridged dark piece in the arm (b64). Element 4211679 is used twice: in the second arm and in the lamp.
The red hard hat (element 383321) uses catalogue type lego-minifig-hardhat. The blue long pin uses its own element ID, lego-4514553.
Cab side panels use a bar port that clips onto the orange clip plates. The wheel hub-to-tire join uses pin/pin-hole ports.
Joined edges mostly use null ports for stud connections because the exact stud positions are not legible in the pictures. Stickers are not modelled.

The four wheels are one repeat: copies 1 and 2 attach to the pins of holder b9, copies 3 and 4 to the pins of holder b10. The two white cones with orange caps are another repeat, attached to the two studs of the yellow plate b54.
Only one model in the booklet (Captain America); the Iron Man/Black Widow/Hulk pages are adverts.

Fix for the V4 port-reuse errors: every part type now has one numbered stud/anti-stud port per real stud position (and side-stud.N for the studs on the face of the grey bracket 6123809), and each connection uses its own port. Studs are numbered row-major, with row 1 at the back of the model and column 1 at the left. Where two parts touch over several studs I record one edge, or two where it helped to show the span. Not every stud contact is listed.
Element IDs from the inventory page are used as type ids (lego-<ID>). Only lego-302326 (feet) was already in the catalogue.

The 14 grey brackets are modelled as a 1x2 plate on top (stud.1-2), anti-studs below, and four studs on one side face. Plates mounted sideways (arm plates, face plates, back plate, ears) push their anti-studs onto those side studs. The head is two rings of 6 brackets around a 2x2 hollow that holds the orange/white/pink core.
Torso top layer (step 5): the brown 2x4 plate, two L-corner plates and the tan 1x2 plate together make the 4x4 footprint that ring 1 and the orange core sit on.

Step 3 sub-assembly is read from small pictures: brown 1x4 on the back blue brick, two blue 1x1 plates at its ends, the clip plate in the middle, then a brown 1x2 and two more blue 1x1 plates stacked on top. This may not be exact.

Hands are blue 2x2 plates pressed onto the bracket side studs. Each carries a tile 1x2 and a brown clip plate on its own studs. The shield clips onto the left (side-clip) hand. Steps 6-7 are low resolution.

The ear stack (steps 15-18) is only roughly resolved. Its tan and blue tiles and plate are placed on distinct side studs of the left (b30/b40) or right (b31/b41) brackets. The copy-2 attach overrides move each of them to the right side.

Leg order is inferred: the 2x2 plate (b56) sits on the underside of the brown body plate, the blue 1x2 bricks hang from its anti-studs, and the black 1x2 feet go below them. The feet stand on base studs 8 and 11 (the exact base positions are a guess). The name tile, the black 1x4 plate with two studs and the 1x4 tile follow the step 23 inset roughly.

Fixed port-reuse errors: every stud/anti-stud port is now used by at most one edge. The new part types that sit under several parts (white/green/brown plates, blue 2x4 brick, 2x4 brown slope, 3x2 white slope, 2x2 plate with side studs) now declare numbered stud/anti-stud ports. Port lists on these types are abbreviated to the ports actually used, not every stud.

Piece Element IDs on the inventory page are blurry. Some are best guesses, for example 4211396 vs 4211397 for the head plate, and 4107762 as a green 1x2 tile. Catalogue types are used only where the ID and description match.

Which exact stud each piece sits on is an approximation of the pictured stacking. The body is built in steps that flip the model (b1-b21), and the base (b39-b59) is layered in ways the small drawings don't fully show. Stud numbers were chosen so each port is used once.

Steps 4 and 5 of the body put one pin through each of four tan Technic bricks (b5, b6, b10, b11). Each leg's Technic brick turns on one of these pins (revolute), so the leg repeat uses attach overrides for copies 2-4.
The head joins the body by its 2x4 plate sitting on the neck 2x3 plate. The tongue clip plate (b35) clips onto the mudguard bar (b20).

The finished sheep just rests on the base, since page 27 has no build step. The four feet are modelled as contact edges to green tile b53. This is a real contact and not a mistake, so the edges are kept.
The grey pin with stud (b37, step 14) goes into the rear hole of b4, and the 1x2 plate (b38, step 15) sits on its stud.

Instruction numbering restarts for each submodel. The body is pages 3-7, the head is pages 8-12 (step 10 attaches it), the legs are steps 12-13, then the pin, the tail plate and the base (pages 16-26).

The PDF has no inventory pages (only picture steps), so Element IDs are not visible. Catalogue types were chosen by shape and colour is in props. Pieces with no close catalogue match were given descriptive new lego-* type ids.
Several steps (3, 4, 6, 12, 14, 20) show many similar pieces from oblique views; exact piece counts and stud positions are best estimates. Ports used for placement are approximate.
Step 3 sub-assembly: black plate with two stacks of dark red plates and a round plate. Wings rest on the stacks.

The lower wings (steps 10-11) are modelled as a tapered wing plate plus a 2x6 extension each. The upper wing (page 20) is a yellow 2x4 plate, two tapered wings, two extensions, two round plates and a yellow wedge, resting on two dark red struts.
The accessories in step 19 (dark red piece, sextant, binoculars) are placed loosely in the cockpit. Their attachment studs are guessed.
Stickers on the final step are not parts and are omitted.

Pilot legs changed to catalogue type lego-4551179 and torso to lego-4551188 (a matching pair with hip ports), replacing the unreal part numbers. The exact colours (dark grey legs, black jacket with red stripes) are in props only. The pilot sits on the seat via a contact edge.
Goggles port is a hinge kind. The nose round plate is a new type with an axle-hole so it fits the axle. The red base plate, hull pieces and wings have enough distinct ports, so no stud is used twice.

Pilot is built first (page 2) and seated in the cockpit at the end (step 26). The axle end port end.1 is shared by several parts threaded on the same axle (cowling, bush, propeller, nose plate); this is an intentional multi-part join on one axle.
